Limits on what an image may make zupix allocate

Source: R/limits.R
pix_limits.Rd

Images are hostile input: a small file can declare a huge image. zupix reads an image's header, checks it against these limits, and only then allocates anything, so a breach raises a zupix_limit_error (see zupix-conditions) before any pixel memory exists.

Usage

pix_limits(
  max_side = getOption("zupix.max_side", 65535L),
  max_pixels = getOption("zupix.max_pixels", 1e+08),
  max_bytes = getOption("zupix.max_bytes", 2^31),
  max_metadata = getOption("zupix.max_metadata", 16 * 2^20)
)

Arguments

max_side

The largest width or height, in pixels. The default, 65,535, is JPEG's own maximum.

max_pixels

The largest width * height. The default is 10^8.

max_bytes

The most memory one decode may use: the R result, its working copy and the decoder's work buffer together. The default is 2 GiB. A 10^8-pixel RGBA image needs 3.2 GB as a double array but 400 MB as a nativeRaster. Inputs read from a file or connection are also capped at this size.

max_metadata

The most bytes of metadata (ICC profile, EXIF) one image may carry. The default is 16 MiB.

Value

A zupix_limits object, to pass as the limits argument of the readers.

Details

The defaults can be changed for a session with the options zupix.max_side, zupix.max_pixels, zupix.max_bytes and zupix.max_metadata.

Examples

pix_limits()
#> <zupix_limits>
#>   max_side      65,535
#>   max_pixels    100,000,000
#>   max_bytes     2,147,483,648
#>   max_metadata  16,777,216
pix_limits(max_pixels = 1e6)
#> <zupix_limits>
#>   max_side      65,535
#>   max_pixels    1,000,000
#>   max_bytes     2,147,483,648
#>   max_metadata  16,777,216
